senses.definition: Being between two extremes, or in the middle of a range.

quotes.text: The yawning gap in neuroscientists’ understanding of their topic is in the intermediate scale of the brain’s anatomy. Science has a passable knowledge of how individual nerve cells, known as neurons, work. It also knows which visible lobes and ganglia of the brain do what. But how the neurons are organised in these lobes and ganglia remains obscure.

senses.definition: An automobile that is larger than a compact but smaller than a full-sized car.
(chemistry) Any substance formed as part of a series of chemical reactions that is not the end-product.

subsenses.definition: (chemical industries) Any such substance that is produced and sold to commercial customers (business-to-business sales) as an input to other chemical processes.

senses.definition: (motor racing) A kind of tyre with relatively light grooving, used for conditions between fully dry and fully wet.
examples: Light rain was coming so he chose intermediate tyres.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To mediate, to be an intermediate.
(transitive) To arrange, in the manner of a broker.
examples: Central banks need to regulate the entities that intermediate monetary transactions.
